# Grupo Ferra — scope v3

*Client · Monterrey · ~200 people · operations director: Daniela Ruiz · board decision in two days*

## Where we are
Phase one is done: five planners in operations use an AI assistant on their own order spreadsheets. Time to answer a customer order went from **two days to four hours**. No new software, same people, 28 hours of my time over six weeks.

## Phase two (what the board decides)
- **Who:** the same five planners plus purchasing (four people).
- **How long:** four weeks, two sessions a week, the rest on their own.
- **What changes:** paid against measured use. The metric is theirs to pick; my proposal is *orders answered the same day*. If it does not move, they do not pay.
- **Price:** fixed, written in the proposal they already have. Not in this note on purpose.

## Daniela's two questions (two days ago)
1. *What happens with our customers' data if we use the tool?*
2. *What do we do if the team stops using it in three months?*

## The answers (drafted)
Daniela, here are the two answers, short so you can take them to the board as they are.

1. Data. Nothing leaves Ferra: the tool runs on company accounts, customer data trains no model, and we put it in writing in the contract, with the clause your lawyer already reviewed in phase one.

2. Adoption. If in three months the team isn't using it, the problem is mine, not theirs. That is why phase two is paid against measured use: five planners, four weeks, the metric you choose. If it doesn't move, you don't pay.

If it helps the board, I'm available the day of the meeting at whatever time you say.

Pablo

## The ethical test, applied
Is the person running after the machine or the reverse? The planners chose the workflow. Who answers if it goes wrong? I do, in writing. Did we ask the one it lands on? Yes: the planners, before Daniela.

## What I would not do
Sell phase three now. Boredom test: if phase two becomes me operating their spreadsheets, I am operating, not designing. Phase two has to end with them not needing me.
